purpose: Naloxegol is used to treat constipation caused by opioid pain medications in adults with chronic non-cancer pain. It helps get your bowels moving again when opioids like hydrocodone, oxycodone, or morphine are slowing things down. It is not meant for people who take opioids for cancer-related pain.
how_it_works: Opioid pain medicines can block the normal movement of your gut, causing constipation. Naloxegol works by blocking the effect of opioids specifically in your intestines, without affecting the pain relief they provide in your brain. Think of it as telling your gut to ignore the opioid's slowing effect, so things can move normally again.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stomach pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas, and vomiting. Some people also experience headaches or sweating. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not take naloxegol if you have a bowel blockage or are at risk for one. It can cause opioid withdrawal symptoms like sweating, chills, runny nose, or irritability — tell your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the drug's levels in your body. Also tell your doctor about all your other medications, as some can interact with naloxegol.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 25 mg taken by mouth once a day in the morning, on an empty stomach. If that dose is not tolerated, your doctor may lower it to 12.5 mg once daily. Swallow the tablet whole or crush and mix with water if needed — do not take it with grapefruit juice.
